subject.title: Feature Request: Memory Trust Tagging by Source

question: What native OpenClaw trust/provenance model should govern durable memory writes and retrieval across memory-core, QMD, session memory, Memory Wiki, and plugin/MCP boundaries?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix requires maintainer choices about non-forgeable trust assignment, durable schema and migrations, public config/API shape, retrieval policy, and how external MCP/plugin implementations relate to native memory.

options.title: Design Native Trust Contract
options.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

options.title: Split To Provenance Foundations First
options.body: Make durable provenance foundations canonical in the related memory provenance issues, then implement trust policy on top of that contract.

options.title: Rely On External MCP For Now
options.body: Document world-model-mcp and similar integrations as optional user paths while leaving native OpenClaw memory without trust policy for now.

recommendation.title: Design Native Trust Contract
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the native security/product tracker and define host-authored trust metadata plus retrieval policy before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest current code-history signal on the memory host SDK, config, and memory-core contract boundary that needs product/security direction.
